knowledge.title_en: Breakevens: How Oil Gets Into Bond Yields
knowledge.body_en:
A nominal Treasury yield splits into a real yield and a breakeven, the inflation rate at which an inflation-linked bond and a nominal bond return the same. Breakevens are traded, so they move with anything that changes the expected price path. Oil is the fastest input: it feeds headline CPI within weeks through gasoline, and markets reprice near-term breakevens almost tick for tick with crude.

That is why an oil spike hits bonds even when growth looks unchanged. Higher breakevens lift nominal yields directly; if the central bank is then expected to lean against it, real yields rise too. Gold often falls in that second case, since real yields are its opportunity cost.
knowledge.why_en: WTI is up 4% and the 10-year yield sits at 5.18% today, while gold has dropped 4.6% on the week.
